_: Hand-resolved v83->v84 sites that no automatic tier can reach, plus source-bug findings. Every entry states the evidence that was checked against the two v84 dumps. resolve.py applies these last; verify.py re-checks them like any other patch.

0x0040013E.evidence: PE COFF Characteristics = e_lfanew + 0x16. e_lfanew is 0x128 in v83 (localhome.exe) and 0x130 in the v84 image, so the field moves 0x128+0x16=0x13E -> 0x130+0x16=0x146. Both images read 0x010F there. Confirmed in v84_mem.bin and v84_mem2.bin.
0x0040013E.caveat: This is a LOADER-TIME flag (IMAGE_FILE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE). Writing it into an already-mapped image does nothing; the source's own comment says as much. Port it into a file patcher, never into the injected DLL.

0x00C08459.evidence: Embedded application manifest. v83 'requestedExecutionLevel' at 0x00C0842A, the level="..." opening quote at 0x00C08459; v84 at 0x00C6142A / 0x00C61459. Constant delta 0x59000, inside the phase-0 anchor envelope. v83 already reads asInvoker (it is a pre-patched localhost repack); v84 still reads requireAdministrator.
0x00C08459.caveat: v83 blanks 0x15 bytes; v84's literal is "requireAdministrator" = 22 bytes to blank. Using the v83 count leaves a stray closing quote and an invalid manifest.

0x00C08463.evidence: closing quote of the same manifest slot, +0xA from 0x00C61459 exactly as in v83.

0x00AFE084.evidence: Three 16-byte-stride IPv4 string slots. Unique such triple in each image: v83 0x00AFE084 holds '192.168.1.109' x3 (already redirected); v84 0x00B4FAC4 holds the stock '63.251.217.4/.3/.2'. Identical in v84_mem.bin and v84_mem2.bin. The sibling data delta 0x51A28 at 0x00AFE8A0 corroborates the region.
0x00AFE084.caveat: Group B. edits\redirect already does this at runtime; port only if you drop that edit.

0x005ABC65.evidence: Six neighbours in 0x005A8B46-0x005ACB39 all resolve at the uniform delta +0x104F3; 0x005ABC65 + 0x104F3 = 0x005BC158, where v84 holds the byte-identical 22-byte block `mov eax,0x258 ; sub eax,[ebx+0x28] ; mov [ebp-0x18],esi ; cdq ; sub eax,edx ; mov ecx,eax ; mov eax,0x320`. Identical in both dumps.

0x005ABC75.evidence: the `mov eax,0x320` at the end of the same block, 0x10 after 0x005BC158, exactly as in v83.

0x008F32CC.evidence: CUIToolTip::MakeLayer. Delta 0x36915 is exactly that of its already-resolved partner 0x008F32DF -> 0x00929BF4. v84 reallocated the register: v83 `mov eax,0x31F ; cmp esi,eax ; jle ; sub eax,ecx ; mov [ebp+0xC],eax`, v84 `mov ecx,0x31F ; cmp esi,ecx ; jle ; sub ecx,eax ; mov [ebp+0xC],ecx`, converging on the identical `mov ecx,[ebx+8] ; add edx,ecx`. The write is +1 = the imm32 in both, so the register change is harmless.
0x008F32CC.caveat: register-reallocated site: the shape check must compare operand geometry, not the register name. That is what the "regalloc": true flag switches on.

0x009B76BD.evidence: Only ONE `mov [ebp-x], 0xFFFFFED4` exists in the whole 0x3310-wide monotone band between 0x009A3E7F (+0x44F76) and 0x009DFCF0 (+0x48286). v83 `mov [ebp-0x30],-300 ; mov [ebp-0x2C],-200 ; mov [ebp-0x28],300`; v84 `mov [ebp-0x34],-300 ; mov [ebp-0x30],-200 ; mov [ebp-0x2C],300 ; mov [ebp-0x28],200`. Same value sequence, frame offsets shifted 4 (one extra local), one extra trailing store. Delta 0x474A5, inside the band. Identical in both dumps.

0x009B76CB.evidence: the `mov [ebp-x], 0x12C` of the same triple, at the same delta 0x474A5.

0x0045B337.evidence: CAvatarMegaphone. v83 `push 0x320 ; push eax ; mov [ebp-0x14],eax ; movsd ; call [ecx+0x90]`; v84 0x0045D3DA `push 0x384 ; push eax ; mov [ebp-0x10],eax ; movsd`. Same block, and v84 raised the literal 800 -> 900 which is why every byte-matching tier missed it. Delta 0x20A3 sits inside the bracket set by 0x0045A5CB (+0x209F) and 0x0045B417 (+0x20A5). Identical in both dumps.
0x0045B337.caveat: v84's baseline here is 900, not 800. The Ezorsia value (m_nGameWidth) is still what you want, but be aware v84 already widened this element.

0x0062FC4A.evidence: IWzGr2DLayer::GetCanvas logo block. Seven sites in 0x0062EE54-0x0062F9CB all resolve by T1 at a uniform delta +0x1549A; 0x0062FC4A + 0x1549A = 0x006450E4, where v84 holds the byte-identical 14-byte block `push 0x258 ; push 0x320 ; push ebx ; push ebx ; push esi ; call [eax+0x8C] ; cmp eax,ebx ; jge`. Only two such blocks remain unclaimed in v84 (0x006450E4, 0x006452FD) matching v83's two (0x0062FC4A, 0x0062FE63) in order. Identical in both dumps.

0x0062FE63.evidence: second of the two remaining logo blocks, same uniform delta +0x1549A, byte-identical 14-byte block.

0x008D1D50.evidence: CUIStatusBar::OnCreate. v83 0x008D1D50 = `push 0x242 ; push 0x320 ; push esi ; push esi ; lea eax,[ebp-0x14] ; push eax`; v84 0x00906C07 = `push 0x242 ; push 0x320 ; push edi ; lea eax,[ebp-0x18] ; push edi ; push eax ; mov byte[ebp-4],0x7B ; call 0x61283A`. Only TWO `push 0x242 ; push 0x320` pairs exist in v84's 0x00906000-0x00907400, matching v83's two (0x008D1D50, 0x008D1FF4), in the same order. Identical in both dumps. The T3 hit that previously claimed 0x0090487E for this site was rejected as a collision with 0x008CFD4B.
0x008D1D50.caveat: delta 0x34EB7 is slightly ABOVE its neighbours' band: v84 REMOVED a couple of bytes between this block and the next (v83 gap 0x2A4 -> v84 gap 0x185). Monotonicity is a strong heuristic here, not a law.

0x008D1D55.evidence: the `push 0x320` immediately after 0x00906C07, exactly as in v83.

0x008D1FF4.evidence: second of the two `push 0x242 ; push 0x320` pairs in v84's status-bar region, matching v83's second (0x008D1FF4). v84 0x00906D8C = `push 0x242 ; push 0x320 ; push edi ; lea eax,[ebp-0x18] ; push edi ; push eax ; mov byte[ebp-4],0x82 ; call 0x61283A` -- same block shape as 0x00906C07, different unwind-state index, as expected for the second copy.

0x008D217C.evidence: AdjustStatusBarInput cave. v83 displaces 9 bytes `push 0x16 ; push edi ; lea ecx,[esi+0xCD0]`; v84 0x00906EBE displaces 9 bytes `push 0x16 ; push edi ; lea ecx,[esi+0xD08]` -- tiles exactly, same instruction count. The CUIStatusBar member offset moved +0x38, and the independently T2-resolved 0x008D247B -> 0x009071BD shows the identical +0x38 shift (0xCD4 -> 0xD0C), which corroborates this address from a second site. Delta 0x34D42 equals 0x008D247B's exactly.
0x008D217C.cave_body_edit: REQUIRED: the naked asm in AdjustStatusBarInput replays `lea ecx,[esi+0x0CD0]`. For v84 that must become `lea ecx,[esi+0x0D08]`.

0x00BE273C.evidence: No absolute code xref exists for this dword, but its sibling 0x00BE2738 resolved by xref to 0x00C3BA80 and 0x00BE2DF0/0x00BE2DF4 resolved to 0x00C3C138/0x00C3C13C -- all three at the same delta 0x59348. 0x00BE273C = 0x00BE2738 + 4 therefore maps to 0x00C3BA84.

0x008D1F65.evidence: AdjustStatusBarBG. Four independent lines, all checked in both dumps. (1) MEMBER: v83 reads the object through `add eax,0xCCC` at 0x008D1F46; v84 through `lea ecx,[esi+0xD04]` at 0x00906D3C. 0xCCC+0x38=0xD04, and +0x38 is the measured shift for every CUIStatusBar member above ~0xC40 (v83 0xCD0->v84 0xD08 and 0xCD4->0xD0C are the two confirmed cave sites; the 0xCD4 group is 11 sites in v83 and 11 in v84 in the same order). (2) SEH ALIGNMENT: the `mov [ebp-4],state` unwind markers run 0x72,0x73,0x74,0x73,0x75,0x76,0x75,0x77,0x78,0x77,0x79,0x7A,0x7B in v83 and 0x7E,0x7F,0x80,0x7F,0x81,0x82,0x81,0x83,0x84,0x83,0x85,0x86,0x87 in v84 -- a constant +0xC with NO insertion or deletion across the whole 0x008D1E7B..0x008D2185 / 0x00906CE5..0x00906EC7 span. The anchor at the far end of that run is P248 0x008D217C->0x00906EBE, already verified independently. 0x008D1F65 and 0x00906D39 sit in the corresponding sub-block (v83 0x73/0x74, v84 0x7F/0x80). (3) PREAMBLE: both blocks construct the same pair of ZXString temporaries into [ebp-0x28] and [ebp-0x50]/[ebp-0x4c] with the same `push ebx ; lea ecx ; call <ctor>` twice, and both are followed by `mov ecx,eax ; call`. (4) ARGUMENT POSITION: 0x16 is the same argument in the same position in both. Ordinally it is also the 2nd of 3 `push 0x16` in each image's status-bar region, which is how phase 1 guessed it -- that alone was NOT sufficient evidence, because the 2nd v84 site has the shape of the *Input* cave, not the BG cave.
0x008D1F65.cave_body_v84: push nStatusBarY ; push edi ; lea ecx,[esi+0x0D04] ; jmp [dwStatusBarBackgroundPosRetn]
0x008D1F65.caveat: REDESIGNED CAVE, NOT A RE-POINT. v84 recompiled the call: v83 was a vtable call `call [ecx+0x90]` taking both ZXStrings BY VALUE (4x movsd each), v84 is a direct thiscall `call 0x428CEF` with `this = esi+0xD04` taking them BY POINTER. So the v83 displaced run (`push 0x16 ; movsd ; push 0` = 5 bytes) does not exist in v84. The v84 run is `push 0x16 ; push edi ; lea ecx,[esi+0xD04]` = 2+1+6 = 9 bytes, which is the SAME shape as AdjustStatusBarInput. Cave size is therefore 9 (5-byte jmp + 4 nops), retn 0x00906D42. Phase 1's note proposed `nops 3` -- that is arithmetically impossible, a 5-byte E9 does not fit in 3 bytes, and 3 was the only other whole-instruction tiling at this address. UNPROVEN: that 0x16 still drives the background layer's Y in v84's UI.wz. The address, the tiling and the body are proven at the binary; the visual effect is not.

not_portable_as_is._: Empty. 0x008D1F65 (AdjustStatusBarBG) lived here through phase 1; phase 2 resolved and redesigned it -- see sites/0x008D1F65. Nothing else in the set is a known-unportable construct; the remaining gaps are unresolved addresses.

P113.fault: NOT A RESOLUTION CONSTANT. The site is `push 0x10 ; push 0x258 ; call 0x403196 ; pop ecx ; pop ecx ; mov [edi],eax` -- a two-argument cdecl allocator returning a pointer. The 600 is a sizeof, and Ezorsia matched it purely because the literal happens to be 600.
P113.proof: v84's counterpart is 0x005F8BCF, delta 0x14C2F, inside the monotone band [0x10789, 0x14E98] and the only `push 0x10 ; push <~600> ; call 0x403196` in it. v84 raised the literal to 0x260 = 608, while EVERY genuine resolution site in the set still reads 600. A structure grew by 8 bytes; a screen did not.
P113.fix: DO NOT PORT. Writing m_nGameHeight (720) there over-allocates by 112 bytes and is merely wasteful at 1280x720, but at any height below 608 it under-allocates and corrupts the heap. Dropped from the shipping set.

P031.fault: The instruction at 0x004D59B2 is `cmp ecx, 0x258` (81 F9 58 02 00 00) -- a 6-byte form whose imm32 starts at +2, not +1. The comment (`mov eax,800`) describes the neighbouring 0x004D599D, not this site.
P031.as_shipped: writes the 4 value bytes over 81 [F9 58 02 00], leaving 81 D0 02 00 00 00 = `adc eax, 2`, then a stray `add byte ptr [esi+0xE], bh`. Register and memory corruption, not a crash, which is why it survived.
P031.fix: offset 2, value m_nGameHeight (the operand really is the 600 height compare)

P311.fault: The instruction is `add eax, 0xFFFFFED4` (05 D4 FE FF FF) -- imm32 at +1, not +2. It is an `add`, not a `push`; the comment is wrong too.
P311.as_shipped: writes one byte past the immediate, corrupting the following `cmp dword ptr [esi+0x28], eax`.

P158.fault: 0x0064061D is `idiv ecx` (F7 F9) -- two bytes, no immediate at all. The `mov ecx, 0x258` the comment means is at 0x00640618, which the previous source line already patches.
P158.as_shipped: overwrites F7 [F9 8B 45 E0] -> F7 D0 02 00 00 = `not eax` plus garbage, directly on the divisor setup.
P158.fix: DELETE. 0x00640618+1 already applies the intended height. Do not port this operation.

P302_P304.source: Memory::WriteInt(0x009F7079, m_nGameHeight) // dd 600   AND   Memory::WriteInt(0x009F7078 + 1, m_nGameHeight)
P302_P304.fault: Not destructive, but redundant: 0x009F7078 is `push 0x258` so its imm32 IS 0x009F7079. The source writes the same two dwords twice under two spellings (lines 290/291 and 311/312).
P302_P304.fix: keep one spelling (0x009F7078 + 1 / 0x009F707D + 1); drop the other so the patch set has one row per real operand.

manifest_fill.fault: count is computed from the v83 literal length. v84's literal is one byte longer -- see the 0x00C08459 site entry above.

elevation_noop.fault: Intent is HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE (0x80000002) -> HKEY_CURRENT_USER (0x80000001) on a `push imm32`. In localhome.exe the push already reads 0x80000001, so the write is a no-op there. Not a bug in the source, but it means these three cannot be validated against this v83 reference.
elevation_noop.fix: no change; group A, already covered by edits\bypass.

ip_fill.fault: cosmetic: the count expression subtracts two 0x006Fxxxx addresses while the target is 0x00AFxxxx. The difference (0x2E) is what is used, so behaviour is correct, but the expression is a copy-paste artefact.
